problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},$ where $t\ge 1$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=4$ and velocity $v=0$ when $t=1,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t\ge 1.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Position Function of a Particle Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=4{e}^{4t}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=\frac{1}{2}$ and velocity $v=1$ when $t=0$, calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 4{e}^{4t}\text{d}t \\  & ={e}^{4t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & ={e}^{4t}+C \\ 1 & ={e}^{4(0)}+C \\ 1 & =1+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)={e}^{4t}.$ 

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4t}+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4t}+K \\ \frac{1}{2} & =\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4(0)}+K \\ \frac{1}{2} & =\frac{1}{4}+K \\ K & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4t}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4t}+1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
